name: Hiroka Furuuchi
affiliation: Graduate School of Economics, Kobe University
research_interests: Macroeconomics, Automation, Labor Share, and Inequality

papers.title: The Elasticities of Substitution Between Capitals and Labors and the Aggregate Labor Share
papers.summary: A dynamic general equilibrium analysis of capital-labor substitution, ICT capital deepening, the aggregate labor share, and the skill premium in Japan.

papers.title: Foreign Labor and Automation in a Small Open Economy: A Quantitative Model for Japan
papers.summary: A quantitative small open economy model for Japan that studies how foreign labor affects automation adoption and intensity, with remittances and external balance shaping the aggregate response.

papers.title: Carbon pricing, licensing, and a persistent dirty equilibrium
papers.summary: A dynamic general equilibrium model of education, clean research, and costly technology adoption, examining how licensing affects the persistence of a dirty equilibrium and the effectiveness of carbon pricing.

papers.title: Automation, Skill Choice, and Wage Inequality
papers.summary: Research on the interaction between automation, skill choice, and wage inequality.

papers.title: Human Capital Heterogeneity, Occupational Choice, and R&D in a Dynamic General Equilibrium Model
papers.summary: A dynamic general equilibrium model of heterogeneous human capital and occupational choice between production and R&D, examining how the allocation of human capital affects innovation and aggregate economic dynamics.
